video.title: The Most Profitable One-Man Business You’ve Never Heard Of

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Alex, who runs a forestry mulching and land-clearing business near Cincinnati. Alex explains how he spotted local demand, priced jobs, used video ads and YouTube to educate leads, and scheduled large farm jobs in winter to reduce seasonality. He reports strong revenue and margins, while also describing equipment costs, maintenance, and other Bobcat services such as snow removal. The central takeaway is that clear local demand and a video-led sales funnel helped a capital-intensive, physical service business grow quickly; the work itself still depends on people and machinery.

speakers.name: Alex
speakers.description: Owner of Brushworks Co; surname not stated.

ideas.name: Forestry mulching and land clearing
ideas.one_liner: Use a forestry-equipped Bobcat and mulching head to clear overgrown land for residential and commercial customers.
ideas.business_model: Per-job service, priced by day initially and later by quarter acre with density and terrain adjustments; additional grapple work and other upsells.
ideas.customer: Landowners with overgrown property, including residential customers and owners of large farms; commercial work is also discussed as a scaling opportunity.
ideas.problem: Property becomes unusable as invasive honeysuckle and other growth spreads. Customers may not know forestry mulching exists and may otherwise pay tree services to clear land by hand.
ideas.offer: Clear woods and overgrown land with a forestry mulcher, leaving a layer of mulch that breaks down over time. The crew also offers grapple work and asks customers to clear debris beforehand.

pricing.model: Initially per day; later priced per quarter acre, adjusted for three brush-density tiers and three terrain tiers.

price_points.label: Rate they moved to early on
Approximate price for three acres at tier-two density

pricing.notes: The quarter-acre base price and terrain multipliers are not stated. The guest says customers can be quoted by the day when starting out.

acquisition_channels.details: They ran vertical video ads on Meta/Facebook, targeted within about 50 miles of their area, and sent viewers to the website, which featured their YouTube channel. They reported a $20 cost per lead.

quote.text: So, essentially, we do a meta ad to capture their attention. Only video ads. Only video. Vertical.
quote.speaker: Alex

acquisition_channels.details: They used videos to explain what forestry mulching is, show the process and results, and build trust before a prospect contacted them.

quote.text: So we show them what it is, show them how it's done. They can see what to expect on a job, what it looks like when we show up
quote.speaker: Alex

acquisition_channels.details: They researched hundreds of local search terms, including customer wording such as “clear my woods” and “open up my land,” to assess demand. The transcript does not say they acquired customers through organic search.

quote.text: I did a lot of keyword research on it just looking into you know what if people are searching clear my land
quote.speaker: Alex

ideas.delivery: Alex goes out to quote and marks the area to be cleared. One operator then arrives with the forestry-equipped machine and runs it through the marked area. They ask customers to remove metal, tires, and other debris; if the customer does not, the crew does that work as billable time.
unit_economics_claims: Alex reported about $3,300 as the average job size.
Alex reported a $20 cost per lead and about 49% of quotes closing.
For a roughly $6,000 job, the host estimated about $4,000 profit; Alex agreed with the calculation.
Alex reported spending about $80–$100 per day on diesel and setting aside about 8% for repairs.
Alex reported gross profit of about 70% in the first operating period and net profit of about 40% later.
ideas.startup_cost: Alex financed the first machine and attachment with about $5,000 down, paid about $11,000 cash for a trailer, and bought a used truck for about $8,000. He said a used first machine cost about $74,000 and the first used attachment cost $15,000; the transcript does not give a full startup-cost total.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: The first deal closed two days after ads were published; the first job was about $6,500.

acquisition.how: Agents could help produce ad variants, manage targeting, and route inbound leads, with a person checking the videos, local targeting, and ad spend.

onboarding.how: A person currently visits properties, assesses density and terrain, marks the area, and prepares the operator.

delivery.how: A person must operate heavy machinery and handle site conditions; this is physical work.

billing.how: Billing tools could handle invoices and payments, but the transcript does not describe their billing process.

support.how: Customer questions about property, debris, timing, and results require human judgment.

uk_applicability.notes: The service and video-led local marketing could work in the UK, but demand, equipment financing, land access, and environmental or wildlife rules would need local adaptation.

risks: Forestry mulching wears equipment and parts; Alex says used equipment can be hard to assess and recommends starting with a new machine and warranty.
Metal, tires, and barbed wire can damage teeth or equipment, so the work area needs checking.
Fuel, repairs, insurance, machine payments, suitable towing capacity, and a CDL for some equipment combinations add operating costs and constraints.
Weather and wet ground affected the business's season; Alex adapted by booking suitable large farm properties for winter.
The work is physical, equipment-dependent, and cannot be run unattended.

Use a keyword tool to compare local search demand with a familiar service such as concrete work.
Check the likely service radius; Alex used about 50 miles around his area.

steps: Run vertical video ads that show the problem and the visible before-and-after result.

Route interested viewers to the website contact form.

warnings.warning: Forestry mulching is hard on equipment; Alex says used-machine condition can be difficult to determine and recommends new equipment with a warranty.

quote.text: The reason is is because forestry can be hard on equipment and and it's hard to determine what you're getting.

warnings.warning: Metal, tires, and barbed wire in a work area can damage machine teeth or equipment.

quote.text: You don't want to hit metal. So before a job, we'll go through and make sure all the metal's picked up.

lessons.lesson: Research how customers describe their problem, not only the industry's technical terms; the guest found demand in phrases like “clear my land” and “get rid of this honeysuckle.”

quote.text: They're not as like lane clearing and forestry watching are more the commercial terms. Honeysuckle invasion.

lessons.lesson: A visible service can benefit from video that shows the problem, the process, and the finished result before the sales visit.

quote.text: Most people don't know what forest streaming is, what land clearing is. So, we show them what it is, show them how it's done.
quote.speaker: Alex

lessons.lesson: Compare local search demand with the number of providers before committing to a service category.

quote.text: So people were searching for these terms and so that's how I just decided hey this is going to work.
quote.speaker: Alex

lessons.lesson: A customer can value an outcome emotionally as well as financially; Alex's first customer wanted the property to look as it did in childhood.

quote.text: So she wanted the property that she grew up in to look like it did when she lived there when she was a kid.
quote.speaker: Alex

lessons.lesson: Start with a pricing method that is easy to quote, then add detail as operational scale requires it.

quote.text: If you wanted to start out like we did, you could also just do it by day.
quote.speaker: Alex

lessons.lesson: Plan seasonal work ahead by asking flexible customers about timing and offering a discount for suitable off-season jobs.

quote.text: I'll offer them a 10% discount for us to move that to the winter.
quote.speaker: Alex

lessons.lesson: A machine-based business can add adjacent services to use equipment in more conditions or seasons, but each service still requires operators and suitable attachments.

quote.text: There's a million things you can do with a Bobcat. I mean, there's hundreds of different attachments
quote.speaker: Alex

lessons.lesson: Include job-preparation instructions in customer communications and define how extra cleanup time is billed.

quote.text: If they don't do that, that's fine. We'll do it. It's just that's part of the billable time.
quote.speaker: Alex

lessons.lesson: Treat reported revenue, profit, and growth projections as separate measures; the host initially described gross profit as net profit, and Alex corrected the distinction.

quote.text: Yeah. That's incredible. Um, now let's gross profit. Gross profit. Okay. Gross profit. Yeah. Yeah. Not net.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner and Alex

evidence_quality.rationale: The guest describes his own operating business with specific processes, equipment, pricing, customer acquisition, and financial figures. The numbers are self-reported, some are approximate, and the host makes several calculations or projections that are not independently verified. The transcript includes auto-caption errors and conversational corrections.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: The host reads a sponsored endorsement for Bizzy, an LLC formation and compliance service, and says he uses it. The guest's Brushworks business is not presented as a course or software promotion.
